body:
Controller confirmed by the machine owner (MisterMaker on Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-20): an **Estlcam controller board running Estlcam's own control software**. This is Christian Knüll's German Estlcam, not grbl or the Ooznest BlackBox.

What this means for the machine file:
- The post is not grbl. Estlcam's PC software drives the board directly, and external G-code goes through Estlcam's own control program.
- Still to confirm, from Estlcam's own documentation or a test file run by the owner:
  - which G-code words its control program accepts from other CAM programs (arcs as G2/G3 with I/J or R, G90/G91, units, spindle words, comments, tool changes)
  - its line-length and decimal limits
  - whether it needs a specific file extension
- Until then, the machine file should point at a conservative 3-axis post. Its programs should use only G0/G1/G2/G3 with I/J, G21 or G20, G90, M3/M5 and a feed, with no canned cycles or cutter compensation, so that the owner can test them.

More from the owner (MisterMaker, relayed 2026-11-20):
- **Frame and drive:** a WorkBee **1500 x 1000** (he thinks), driven by **TR8 trapezoidal lead screws**, not belts. TR8 screws limit rapids and feeds: set conservative maximum feeds in the machine file until he confirms them.
- **Work area: 1200 x 800 mm** (X x Y). Z travel is still to confirm.
- **Spindle: 2.2 kW**, most likely a VFD spindle; he calls it "way overkill". Still to confirm: the rpm range (typical 2.2 kW spindles run about 6,000-24,000 rpm, with poor torque at the low end), and whether Estlcam sets the rpm (S word) or the spindle is run by hand.
- **Controller:** Estlcam board with Estlcam software. He doesn't know which G-code Estlcam accepts from other CAM programs. He notes the hardware is open source. The accepted words still have to come from Estlcam's documentation or a test file he runs.

Estlcam's hardware page (https://www.estlcam.de/hardware.php, read 2026-11-20; German) says:
- **Boards:** Estlcam's own controller boards are open-source hardware: a KiCAD 8 project, free for personal and commercial use.
- **Variants:** "Terminal Adapter" (XL, M, Light) and LPT/parallel-port adapters, built on an **AVR64DB64** microcontroller.
- **Firmware:** the page welcomes ports of GRBL to the boards, as long as the bootloader is kept, but it gives no firmware licence.
- **Not covered:** none of the pages read (hardware, index, estlcam, changelog) says which G-code from other CAM programs Estlcam runs, which words it accepts, or how the spindle is controlled. Those still need Estlcam's manual or help pages, or a test file run by the owner.
